Repo: /home/mudathir/all/cvc5/mudathir (cvc5, branch lazy). Uncommitted changes: run
"git diff" there. New feature: option arith-liastar-main-solver moves the lazy LIA* cell
enumeration from a per-lambda subsolver into the MAIN solver. Design (see MainEnum in
src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.h and mainSolverCheckStar/advanceStage/
emitDriverLemma/getModelDisjunct/getMainEnum/addEnumLemma in liastar_extension.cpp):
- lambda bound vars -> fresh integer skolems y; base(y) = predicate (ites/nots removed) + y>=0.
- Stage guards: h_0 => base(y); per discovered cone-disjunct D_k a fresh h_k with
  h_k => h_{k-1} and h_k => not(D_k(y)); en.guard is the current h_k; each h is
  ensureLiteral'd and preferPhase'd true. h_0 additionally gets a split lemma.
- Driver lemma per (literal, stage): literal => (p[v] or star_k or h_k), unguarded,
  where star_k = d_lastStarLia[literal] (under-approximation built by processDisjunct)
  and p[v] is the vector predicate. Claimed satisfiability-preserving.
- Each full-effort round: catch up stages for cones discovered via other literals; if
  guard fixed false at level 0 (Valuation::isFixed) -> emit exact equivalence
  (processDisjunct complete=true); if guard true in SAT assignment -> read the cell from
  arithModel via getModelDisjunct (substitute+rewrite each atom of base; equality atoms
  false in model become strict inequalities; skolems missing from arithModel fall back to
  TheoryArith::getCandidateModelValue), dedupe against d_lazyCones, advanceStage, then
  processDisjunct(false) emits the guarded equivalence g_k => (literal = star_k) and
  deactivates the previous g; then emitDriverLemma for the new stage.
- Tests: all 9 regress1/arith/liastar tests pass in this mode (Debug), and in the other
  three modes (accumulate/push-pop/eager); unit test passes.
Focus ONLY on problems introduced by the new main-solver mode (not pre-existing issues in
the subsolver paths). Report findings with concrete code references.
A reviewer (lens termination-progress) claims:
Title: Unguarded driver lemmas share per-lambda multiplier skolems across literals (pre-existing root, surfaced by the new drivers)
Detail: emitDriverLemma asserts d_lastStarLia[literal] unguarded (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1026-1034). The star formulas for different literals over the SAME lambda share the multiplier skolems mu/l, because getStarConstraints caches per-cone constraints and (point, rays) contributions keyed by lambda (d_starConstraints/d_lambdas, liastar_extension.cpp:673-731) while building per-literal sum constraints `v_i = Sigma contributions(mu)` over the SAME skolems. Once coverage completes and the guards are forced false, two positively asserted literals with different vectors v1 != v2 that both need the star branch make their drivers jointly require v1 = Sigma(mu) and v2 = Sigma'(mu) over shared mu, which over-constrains (independent witnesses are intended) and can produce a spurious UNSAT on a satisfiable instance. The root cause (per-lambda skolem sharing) is pre-existing -- the subsolver path's complete equivalences literal = star have the same defect -- so this is flagged for awareness rather than as a regression: the new mode adds more unguarded, never-retractable occurrences of these shared-skolem formulas (one driver per literal per stage) where the subsolver path only exposes unguarded occurrences at completion. Per-literal (not per-lambda) multiplier skolems, or existential closure of the star body, would remove the coupling.
Adversarially verify against the actual code (git diff + files). Is this a REAL problem
introduced by the new main-solver mode? Default isReal=false unless the reasoning reproduces
concretely from the code.

content.text: I have everything needed. Let me do one final check on the exact line numbers cited and confirm the completion-equivalence behavior in both modes at HEAD.

input.reasoning: The reviewer's code-level facts are accurate but the defect is pre-existing, not introduced by the new main-solver mode — as the reviewer's own claim concedes ("pre-existing root... flagged for awareness rather than as a regression"). Verified mechanics: (1) emitDriverLemma (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp:1026-1035) does emit `literal => (p[v] OR d_lastStarLia[literal] OR guard)` as an unguarded, non-retractable lemma. (2) Multiplier skolems ARE shared per lambda: getStarConstraints (lines 673-731) caches per-cone constraints and (point,rays) in d_starConstraints[n[0]]/d_lambdas[n[0]] keyed by the LAMBDA, with mu/l skolems created once per cone (liastar_utils.cpp:1045,1069), while buildSumConstraints (lines 133-158) equates each PER-LITERAL vector to sums over those shared skolems. Two literals over the same lambda with v1 != v2 whose stars are jointly forced imply v1 = Sigma(mu) = v2, a genuine spurious-UNSAT risk (concrete example: p=(x=2 or x=3), v1=4, v2=5 gives 4=2mu1+3mu2=5). HOWEVER: (a) all of this machinery — getStarConstraints per-lambda caching, d_lastStarLia, and the unconditional completion equivalence `literal = star` per literal — exists at HEAD in the lazy subsolver path (HEAD lines 666-693 and lazyHilbert's complete branch, refactored verbatim into processDisjunct:1238); the diff hunks confirm only dispatch, the new MainEnum functions, and a mechanical refactor were added. (b) The driver lemma is strictly weaker than `literal => star` implied by the completion equivalences BOTH modes emit at the same mathematical completion condition (base AND negated cells unsat = subsolver-unsat = guard fixed false), so any instance where drivers force the shared-mu conflict also fails identically in the pre-existing subsolver mode. (c) Pre-completion the drivers force nothing: the stage guard is a free decision literal (only downward implications h_k => h_{k-1}, h_k => not(D_k) from advanceStage:994-1006), and stale drivers' older guards h_j (j<k) remain satisfiable even at completion since base AND not(D_1..D_j) stays sat, so the extra per-stage unguarded occurrences are disjunctively shielded and create no new failure scenario. The eager path is unaffected (getCones builds fresh skolems per literal). Per the task's scope (problems introduced by the new mode only) and the default, isReal=false; the shared-skolem coupling deserves a fix (per-literal multipliers or existential closure) but as a pre-existing lazy-path issue.
